For bipartite graphs, avoiding 4-cycles (C_4) means no two vertices in one part can share more than one common neighbor in the other part. This restricts the number of paths of length 2 to at most C(a,2) + C(b,2), where a and b are the sizes of the two parts. For a+b=17, the maximum is C(8,2) + C(9,2) = 28 + 36 = 64. Since 66 > 64, no bipartite graph can have 28 edges and girth 6.

For non-bipartite graphs, avoiding C_3, C_4, and C_5 imposes even stricter structural constraints. It is a known result in extremal graph theory that the maximum number of edges for a graph on 17 vertices with girth 6 is 26 (and the extremal graphs are bipartite). Therefore, 28 edges is mathematically impossible.
